IGR J0029+5934’s double-peaked 100 day outburst in 2008 is consistent with the standard picture of an outbursting AMSP.

The main takeaway from our work is that
AMXPs are complex objects, and that a multi-wavelength study is essential to understanding the physics of accreting neutron star systems in general.
AMXPs are not just “scaled-up versions” of X-ray novae, and their outbursts are not just scaled-up versions of those of X-ray novæ.
